120	A lion — if we tell him, "How about being a rabbit?"
121	"Act like a
122	rabbit." A lion is a lion, he won't be a rabbit. And if
123	we tell the rabbit, "Maybe be strong like a mighty lion,
124	pounce on everyone, bite them," he's a rabbit.
125	Every animal has its own particular trait. Man
126	gathers within himself the traits of all the animals
127	and he can choose how to direct them. The Mishnah
128	says, "Be bold as a leopard,
129	and light as an eagle, and mighty
130	as a lion." What does all this mean? That you should be like the animals.
131	The intention is to take the central trait. You
132	see that the lion has the trait of strength. You too
133	should be strong. In the Shulchan Aruch it is written, "Strengthen yourself to rise
134	in the morning for the service of the Creator." He went to sleep late after
135	his brother's wedding at night, but he knows the time of
136	the Shema, so that it should not
137	pass. He strengthens himself, washes his hands before dawn, recites the
138	Shema. After that he can sleep a little more, but he must not
139	miss the time of the Shema. He strengthens himself like a lion. Because
140	it is a Torah commandment to recite the Shema at its time.

153	looks when he wants to. The look he has

159	boldness can be used for good or for bad.
160	So here it says:
161	"light as an eagle." The eagle has wings, but you see
162	him when he wants to rise, suddenly, with such
163	lightness, he flies upward. You too must
164	be somewhat nimble. Rise up, move,

171	a person has the choice. You can be like

177	You don't know from which side, why he is cunning,

179	about human beings by comparison to animals. Because
